chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the woman who prays to the side of the man, near to him, he said: 'When there is a place between them of one saddle-bag (cubit), there is no problem.'

key_terms.إِلَى جَنْبِ الرَّجُلِ: To the side of the man, indicating parallel alignment rather than behind.
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible, a common legal phrase indicating validity.
key_terms.مَوْضِعُ رَحْلٍ: The space of a saddlebag, a traditional measure of distance (approx. one cubit) used in fiqh to determine validity of prayer arrangements.

ai.seo_question: What is the required distance between a man and a woman when praying side-by-side?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the spatial requirements for a woman praying in parallel (muqabala) to a man, establishing that a gap of 'mawdi'u rahlin' (roughly a cubit) renders the prayer valid. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that while parallel prayer is permissible, maintaining a modest distance prevents the invalidation caused by excessive closeness or distraction, distinguishing it from the stricter requirements often applied in other schools of thought regarding the Imam's position.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the woman who prays Salāt to the side of the man, near to him. So heasws said: ‘When there was a place between the two of them of one saddle-bag (cubit), so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a woman who performs Salah (prayer) on the side of the man nearby. He (the Imam) said, ‘If there is a distance of one Rahl (yard), it is not harmful.
